thread:
maria_supp: FYI — Acme is seeing a sudden spike of 502s for hosted API around 16:24 UTC. ~30% failures on /v1/generate. Ticket #12345 attached. Can Eng take a look?

opsbot: Incident created INC-2026-237. Alert: edge-proxy 502 rate increased (us-west-2). P95 latency elevated. /incidents/INC-2026-237

dan_sre: On it. Any repro or trace IDs from the customer?

maria_supp: Customer sent a repro curl and a trace id: x-rt-97531. Their curl (simplified):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Account-Billing: <long-base64>" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
They say failures only during bursts (~150-250 rps) and only when billing header present.

tessa_infra: Looking at edge logs now — seeing surge where upstream 'auth-cache' returns 503s then edge starts returning 502s. Snippet: 
```
[16:24:12] edge-proxy: stream reset: upstream_reset_before_response_started, retries_exhausted
[16:24:13] auth-cache: latency=1223ms, queue=47, conn_pool_exhausted=true
[16:24:14] envoy: upstream reset: goaway with error code 2
```
Also multiple h2 GOAWAYs for the auth-cache pool.

dan_sre: Interesting — the customer mentioned a big billing header. Do we have header size/conn limits set? Could be h2 window or conn pool exhaustion if headers are large and we multiplex many streams.

maria_supp: They confirmed they send a ~3KB base64 blob in X-Account-Billing per request (from their SDK).

 tessa_infra: I reproduced locally: send 150 concurrent requests with 3KB X-Account-Billing and you can force the auth-cache pool to exhaust, which leads to stream resets and 502s. Repro steps I used:
1) make a small payload.json (~1KB)
2) export BILLING_HEADER=$(head -c 3072 /dev/urandom | base64)
3) hey -n 500 -c 150 -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Account-Billing: $BILLING_HEADER" -m POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d @payload.json
Observed: auth-cache latency spikes to >1s, conn_pool_active hits max, envoy emits GOAWAYs and edge starts returning 502.

dan_sre: That matches. Two vectors: oversized headers increasing memory/cpu while parsing + h2 conn pool/streams saturating. Also saw increase in retries to upstream, causing head-of-line blocking.

maria_supp: Customer asked for a quick mitigation — they were getting throttled and worried about data loss.

tessa_infra: Short-term mitigations applied: 1) temporarily moved that customer's traffic to a dedicated higher-capacity node pool (done at 16:41 UTC) 2) increased auth-cache connection pool size for the canary region 3) added short circuit to drop/strip billing header if exceeds 2KB for hosted-api (config applied to canary).

maria_supp: Customer reports errors dropped to 0% after migration to dedicated pool. They're asking for root cause and permanent fix.

dan_sre: Next actions (tracked):
- PR to enforce max header size at edge and return 400 when exceeded (PR #4123)
- Improve auth-cache backpressure: queue depth + circuit-breaker tuning
- Add an alert for auth-cache latency >500ms and h2 GOAWAY spikes
- Update SDK guidance: avoid embedding large blobs in headers; send via body or storage link

tessa_infra: Opened infra PR #4123 to add header size enforcement + metrics for per-upstream conn saturation. Rolling canary now (16:58 UTC).

dan_sre: Also we should add a defensive proxy behavior: if upstream returns 503 repeatedly, degrade to 429 or return a clearer error to the client instead of 502. Will propose in the runbook.

maria_supp: I pinged the customer with recommended SDK changes and that we provisioned them temporary dedicated capacity; they'll coordinate to reduce header size.

opsbot: INC-2026-237 marked RESOLVED at 17:10 UTC (mitigated by reroute + header-enforcement canary).

maria_supp: Closing loop internally — will follow up with Product to add header-size best practices to docs and with Support to include a repro checklist for similar cases. :white_check_mark:

tessa_infra: FYI, logs/trace ids for the window saved to /var/log/edge/incidents/INC-2026-237.log and will be attached to the ticket.

dan_sre: Thanks all. Let's keep the alert and PR milestones in the ticket.

maria_supp: Thanks team — customer happy for now, will monitor for regressions.
